Here we want to summarise discussions about the structure of the package, design decisions around functions, and their relationship with the cross-referencing process.

## User journey

For the package design we distinguish two main stages of the cross-referencing process. The first is dedicated to data preparation, validation and exploration. The second is dedicated to analysis and synthesis. See @fig-userjourney for an overview.

```{mermaid}

%%| fig-cap: "Steps of the user journey. Solid green symbols can be completed with the package functions, classes and methods. Dashed symbols require a mix of package functions, other packages, and external tools."

    VALID{"Data<br/>Validation"}:::InPkg
    EXP[Exploration:<br/> Interpreters, rounds, membership values]:::InPkg
    NINT{"No. interpreters<br/> and rounds"}:::InPkg
    ELI1[Within rounds<br/>agreemnet]:::InPkg
    ELI2[Between rounds<br/>entropy metrics]:::InPkg
    
    FILTER["Between rounds<br/>entropy metrics"]:::InPkg
    SYNT[Synthesis]:::InPkg
    OUTP[Outputs]:::Mixed

    subgraph FIRST["Data preparation and exploration"]
        direction LR
        PREP --> VALID
        VALID -->|no| PREP
        VALID -->|yes| EXP -.->|review data if necessary| PREP
    end
    FIRST:::Steps --> SECOND:::Steps
    subgraph SECOND["Analysis"]
        direction LR
        NINT -->|"1 interpreter <br> round"| THIRD;
        NINT -->|"1 interpreter <br> >1 round"| FILTER -->|Filtering| THIRD ;

    end

    classDef Data fill:#f8f9fa,stroke:#1A1A1A,color:#1A1A1A,stroke-width:2px

    classDef Steps fill:#fff,stroke:#853E90,color:#853E90,stroke-width:1px
```

The ecoSynthesis package aims to facilitate the tasks related to these stages of the cross-referencing process. While some task could be completed with the functions, classes and methods defined in this package, there are some task that will require interaction with additional R packages, other tools, and the real world. 

## Functions, classes and methods  

This package includes functions, classes and methods. Some functionality has been **proposed** and tested outside the package development process. Some of these proposals are integrated in **development branches** before they are implemented in the **main branch**.

We use a consistent key to refer to these in all figures [@fig-legend].

```{dot}
//| label: fig-legend
//| fig-cap: "Visual key to functions, classes and methods in different stages of development."
digraph membership {

// classes
node [shape=record fillcolor="#fff4d6", color="#8a5a00", fontcolor="#8a5a00", penwidth=2];
CL[label=<{This is <i>my class</i>|with a description}>]

// methods
node [shape=box fillcolor="#ddffdd", color="#004400", fontcolor="#004400", penwidth=2];
MT[label=<MethodFor(<i>my class</i>)>]

// functions
node [shape=record fillcolor="#e3edfb", color="#1f4e99", fontcolor="#1f4e99", penwidth=2];
FN[label=<{<i>function_name()</i>|with description}>];

node [shape=record fillcolor="#fff4d6", color="#8a5a00", fontcolor="#8a5a00", penwidth=2 style=dashed];
CLWIP[label=<{This is <i>my class</i>|with a description}>]

node [shape=box fillcolor="#ddffdd", color="#004400", fontcolor="#004400", penwidth=2 style=dashed];
MTWIP[label=<MethodFor(<i>my class</i>)>]

node [shape=record fillcolor="#e3edfb", color="#1f4e99", fontcolor="#1f4e99", penwidth=2 style=dashed];
FNWIP[label=<{<i>function_name()</i>|with description}>];

node [shape=record fillcolor="#fff4d6", color="#8a5a00", fontcolor="#8a5a00", penwidth=2 style=dotted];
CLPROP[label=<{This is <i>my class</i>|with a description}>]

node [shape=box fillcolor="#ddffdd", color="#004400", fontcolor="#004400", penwidth=2 style=dotted];
MTPROP[label=<MethodFor(<i>my class</i>)>]

node [shape=record fillcolor="#e3edfb", color="#1f4e99", fontcolor="#1f4e99", penwidth=2 style=dotted];
FNPROP[label=<{<i>function_name()</i>|with description}>];

subgraph cluster_inPkg {
  label = "Main branch"
  FN -> CL -> MT [style=invis]
}
subgraph cluster_WIP {
  label = "Development branches"
  FNWIP -> CLWIP -> MTWIP [style=invis]
}
subgraph cluster_Prop {
  label = "Proposed"
  FNPROP -> CLPROP -> MTPROP [style=invis]
}
CL -> CLWIP -> CLPROP [style=invis]
FN -> FNWIP -> FNPROP[style=invis]
MT -> MTWIP -> MTPROP [style=invis]
}
```

### Core functions

Two core functions ([`lookup_tbl()`](../reference/lookup_tbl.html) and [`membership_tbl()`](../reference/membership_tbl.html)) create the main classes used in the package. All other functions will work with these two main classes. 

:::{.callout-warning}

Documentation of the classes is missing in the R files!

:::

```{dot}
//| label: fig-core
//| fig-cap: "Core functions (blue), classes (gold), methods (green) and their relationships."
digraph membership {

// classes
node [shape=record fillcolor="#fff4d6", color="#8a5a00", fontcolor="#8a5a00", penwidth=2];
MT[label=<{Class <i>membership_tbl</i>|(not documented)}>]
LUT[label=<{Class <i>lookup_tbl</i>|(not documented)}>]

// methods
node [shape=box fillcolor="#ddffdd", color="#004400", fontcolor="#004400", penwidth=2];
LUTP[label=<print(<i>lookup_tbl</i>)>]
MTP[label=<print(<i>membership_tbl</i>)>] 
// 
node [shape=record fillcolor="#e3edfb", color="#1f4e99", fontcolor="#1f4e99", penwidth=2];
LUTF[label=<{<i>lookup_tbl()</i>|Create a lookup table<BR/>for a classification}>];
MTF[label=<{<i>membership_tbl()</i>|Create a membership table}>];

subgraph cluster_prep {
        label="Core functions" style=dashed;
        MT -> MTP [label=<has method>];
        MTF -> MT [label=creates];
        LUTF -> LUT [label=creates];
        LUT -> LUTP [label=<has method>]
    }
}
```

### Data preparation

We propose a couple of simple functions to facilitate the most common data import nad data cleaning steps. 

:::{.callout-important}

```{dot}

//| fig-cap: "Data preparation: functions (blue), classes (gold), methods (green) and their relationship during a cycle of data preparation."
digraph membership {

// classes
node [shape=record fillcolor="#fff4d6", color="#8a5a00", fontcolor="#8a5a00", penwidth=2];
MT[label=<{Class <i>membership_tbl</i>|(not documented)}>]
LUT[label=<{Class <i>lookup_tbl</i>|(not documented)}>]

// methods
node [shape=box fillcolor="#ddffdd", color="#004400", fontcolor="#004400", penwidth=2];
// 
node [shape=record fillcolor="#e3edfb", color="#1f4e99", fontcolor="#1f4e99", penwidth=2];
LUTF[label=<{<i>lookup_tbl()</i>|Create a lookup table<BR/>for a classification}>];
MTF[label=<{<i>membership_tbl()</i>|Create a membership table}>];

node [shape=record fillcolor="#e3edfb", color="#1f4e99", fontcolor="#1f4e99", penwidth=2 style=dotted];
CLEANMT[label=<{<i>clean_membership()</i>|Flag and remove errors from <BR/>membership table}>];

subgraph cluster_prep {
    label="Data preparation cycle";
    READMT -> MTF;
    MT -> CLEANMT  [label=input];
    CLEANMT ->MT
    LUT -> CLEANMT [label=<input<BR/>(optional)>];
    subgraph cluster_main {
        direction=LR
        label="Core functions" style=dashed;
        MTF -> MT [label=creates];
        LUTF -> LUT [label=creates];
    }
}
}
```

However, in many cases data preparation will require wrangling with data formats (e.g. combining or joining data, filtering, modifying records). This can be done effectively inside R (for example with packages from the `tidyverse` collection), or outside R with other tools of preference.

### Validation pipeline

Data validation allows the user to check if the data is valid for further processing. The validation functions are intended to catch common problems and pitfalls that could invalidate the final results. Validation should be completed before moving to data exploration and analysis.  


```{dot}
//| label: fig-validation
//| fig-cap: "Validation pipeline: functions, classes, methods and their relationship during a cycle of validation."
digraph membership {

// classes
node [shape=record fillcolor="#fff4d6", color="#8a5a00", fontcolor="#8a5a00", penwidth=2];
MT[label=<{Class <i>membership_tbl</i>|(not documented)}>]
MC[label=<{Class <i>membership_check</i>|(not documented)}>]
LUT[label=<{Class <i>lookup_tbl</i>|(not documented)}>]

// methods
node [shape=box fillcolor="#ddffdd", color="#004400", fontcolor="#004400", penwidth=2];
MCP[label=<print(<i>membership_check</i>)>] 
// 
node [shape=record fillcolor="#e3edfb", color="#1f4e99", fontcolor="#1f4e99", penwidth=2];
ASMT[label=<{<i>as_membership_tbl()</i>|Coerce a data frame<BR/>to membership_tbl}>];
CHECKMT[label=<{<i>check_membership()</i>|Performs checks on a<BR/>membership table}>];
LUTF[label=<{<i>lookup_tbl()</i>|Create a lookup table<BR/>for a classification}>];
MTF[label=<{<i>membership_tbl()</i>|Create a membership table}>];
VMT[label=<{<i>validate_membership()</i>|Validate a membership table}>];

subgraph cluster_prep {
    label="Data validation pipeline"; 
    MT -> CHECKMT [label=input];
    
    LUT -> CHECKMT [label=<input<BR/>(optional)>];
    CHECKMT -> MC -> VMT;
    
    MC -> MCP [label=<has method>]
    VMT -> ASMT;
    ASMT -> MTF;
    subgraph cluster_main {
        label="Core functions" style=dashed;
        MTF -> MT [label=creates];
        LUTF -> LUT [label=creates];
    }
}
}
```

Positive results of validation means that the process can move to the step of data exploration, negative results indicate that further steps of data preparation are required.


### Exploration

Data exploration includes calculating basic statistics to understand the shape of the data, for example the nr. of interpreters and rounds, or the distribution of membership values.


:::{.callout-important}
## TO DO

Plot classes, summaries and other tools for exploration.

Add figure with existing and proposed functions

:::

Data exploration could lead to identifying gaps or other shortfalls in the data. In such cases, an additional step of data preparation (and validation) might be useful before proceeding with next steps. 

Data exploration will provide the basic data to inform decisions about the analysis and synthesis steps.

### Analysis

Analysis steps will depend on the number of interpreters and rounds. 

With one interpreter and one round, proceed directly to synthesis and outputs.

With one interpreter and multiple rounds, it is possible to analyse how uncertainty (measured as entropy) changes between rounds.

With multiple interpreters it is possible to analyse agreement and disagreement between experts in a single round, and analyse changes in uncertainty and disagreement between rounds. We refer to this process in general as *expert elicitation*, although the specific methods used for the consultation of interpreters can be different in different contexts.
